verses.text: Therefore, since you have been raised with Christ, strive for the things above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God.
Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.
For you died, and your life is now hidden with Christ in God.
When Christ, who is your life, appears, then you also will appear with Him in glory.
Put to death, therefore, the components of your earthly nature: sexual immorality, impurity, lust, evil desires, and greed, which is idolatry.
Because of these, the wrath of God is coming on the sons of disobedience.
When you lived among them, you also used to walk in these ways.
But now you must put aside all such things as these: anger, rage, malice, slander, and filthy language from your lips.
Do not lie to one another, since you have taken off the old self with its practices,
and have put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge in the image of its Creator.
Here there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave, or free, but Christ is all and is in all.
Therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, clothe yourselves with hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.
Bear with one another and forgive any complaint you may have against someone else. Forgive as the Lord forgave you.
And over all these virtues put on love, which is the bond of perfect unity.
Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, for to this you were called as members of one body. And be thankful.
Let the word of Christ richly dwell within you as you teach and admonish one another with all wisdom, and as you sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with gratitude in your hearts to God.
And whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.
Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.
Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh with them.
Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing to the Lord.
Fathers, do not provoke your children, so they will not become discouraged.
Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not only to please them while they are watching, but with sincerity of heart and fear of the Lord.
Whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, for the Lord and not for men,
because you know that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord as your reward. It is the Lord Christ you are serving.
Whoever does wrong will be repaid for his wrong, and there is no favoritism.

context.author: Paul the apostle, with Timothy (1:1)
context.genre: Letter, with a hymn about Christ
context.audience: The church in Colossae, a small town in the Lycus Valley
context.setting: Paul tells the Colossians to seek the things above, where Christ is, because they have died and their life is hidden with Christ. He lists vices to put to death and virtues to put on. He then gives household instructions for wives, husbands, children, parents, slaves, and masters.
context.custom: Roman households included slaves. Paul’s “Whatever you do, work heartily” (v.23) reframes daily work as worship. In the new community, ethnic, religious, and social distinctions no longer divide (v.11).
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 4 continues with prayer, wisdom toward outsiders, and greetings.
context.timelineBible: “Put off the old self” and “put on the new” follows the creation story: renewed in the image of its Creator (v.10, echoing Genesis 1:26-27).
context.sparkNotes: Since you have been raised with Christ, seek the things above. Put to death sexual immorality, greed, anger, and slander. Put off the old self and put on the new, renewed after the image of its Creator, where there is no Greek or Jew, slave or free, but Christ is all. Put on compassion, kindness, humility, meekness, and patience, and above all love. Let the word of Christ dwell richly. Wives, husbands, children, parents, slaves, and masters: do everything as for the Lord.

translation.meaning: To clothe yourself. The virtues are a wardrobe.
Love is what binds all the other virtues together.

otBackground.note: Humans made in God’s image, which the new self restores.
Christ seated at God’s right hand.
The Lord is compassionate and gracious, the pattern for believers.

overview.summary: Raised with Christ, believers put off the old self and put on compassion and love. Daily life, from home to work, is done for the Lord.
overview.settingLine: Paul writes from prison to Colossae.

history.t: Paul speaks to both slaves and masters (3:22-4:1). Onesimus, called one of you (4:9), is sent with Tychicus; most readers think he is the slave of Philemon.
Greeks used barbarian for people who did not speak Greek and often thought of Scythians, from north of the Black Sea, as especially wild. Paul names both to show that no one is outside Christ (3:11).

customs.t: Paul pictures taking off the old self and putting on the new, like a change of clothes (3:9-10). Later churches gave new white robes at baptism, which is later than Paul.
Believers taught each other with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs.

archaeology.t: Tomb inscriptions from Hierapolis, mostly of the 2nd and 3rd centuries AD, name guilds of dyers and weavers. They show how large the cloth trade of the valley was.
Wealthy homes in the cities of Asia had courtyards, mosaics and wall paintings. The Terrace Houses at Ephesus, far to the west, are the best-excavated example.

overview.discussion: Paul says to do everything “in the name of the Lord Jesus.” What ordinary task would feel different if I did it as an offering to him?
overview.book: The letter to the Colossians · 4 chapters. A short, rich letter about the supremacy of Christ.
overview.author: Paul

historicalImage.caption: The Resurrection, a panel of the Isenheim Altarpiece by Matthias Grünewald (1512-16). Colossians 3:1 says that since you have been raised with Christ, you are to strive for the things above, and the chapter goes on to say what that means for daily life.

currentImage.caption: The Terrace Houses on the hillside at Ephesus, a group of wealthy Roman homes with mosaics and painted walls. They show the kind of household, with family, servants and slaves, that Ephesians 5:21-6:9 speaks to.
